_meta.description: Fixture for Fix 7 Portfolio Analyst (Gemini 3 Pro 1M-context, all 30 Internal-30 contracts). One row per deal: short synthetic EX-2.1 excerpt focused on the MAE / MAC carve-out structural language the analyst clusters on. NOT actual contract content — the live path fetches real EX-2.1s via the EdgarTools pipeline already wired for /review-by-deal. deal_ids match the row taxonomy in docs/internal30_deal_bank.md (Calibration-1A post-cutoff core + 1B demo-path + Narrative-12 + one padded synthetic slot to round to 30).
_meta.rounding_note: Internal-30 deal bank distinct rows count to 29 (12 + 5 + 12). One synthetic 'post-cutoff-clean-comparable-b' slot is added below to round to 30 for the Portfolio Analyst's 'one call across 30 contracts' framing. The synthetic row is labeled as such in its `source` field.

contracts.ex21_excerpt: Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect to the extent resulting from (a) general economic or political conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the industries in which Target operates, (c) any acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) any changes in Law or GAAP, or (e) the failure to meet internal projections in itself; provided, that any such effect under clauses (a), (b), (c), or (d) may be taken into account to the extent it disproportionately affects Target relative to its industry peers.

Material Adverse Effect shall exclude effects arising from (a) general economic conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions, (c) acts of war or terrorism or pandemics, (d) changes in law or GAAP, or (e) the announcement of this Agreement; provided that such exclusions in (a)-(d) shall apply only to the extent the effect does not disproportionately affect the Company relative to its peers in the upstream oil and gas industry.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic or political conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the grocery retail industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in applicable Law or GAAP, except in each case of (a)-(d) to the extent such effect disproportionately affects the Company and its Subsidiaries relative to other participants in the grocery retail industry.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect arising from (a) general economic or market conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions affecting the semiconductor design or engineering simulation industries, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, or (e) the failure to meet projections; provided that clauses (a)-(d) apply only to the extent the effect does not disproportionately affect the Company relative to its peers.

Material Adverse Effect excludes effects resulting from (a) general economic, financial market, or political conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the media, entertainment, or streaming industries, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, in each case under (a)-(d) only to the extent such effects do not have a disproportionate impact on the Company relative to comparable industry participants.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic or financial market conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the banking, consumer finance, or payment networks industries, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law (including Reg-Y) or GAAP, except to the extent any such effect disproportionately affects the Company relative to other participants in such industries.

Material Adverse Effect shall exclude effects arising from (a) general economic conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the packaged food industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, or (e) the failure to meet projections; provided that exclusions (a)-(d) apply only to the extent the effect does not have a disproportionate impact on the Company.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic or political conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions affecting the luxury accessories or apparel industries, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, in each case of (a)-(d) only to the extent such effect does not disproportionately impact the Company relative to comparable industry participants.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic or political conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the commercial airline industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law (including aviation regulation) or GAAP, except to the extent such effects disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the airline industry.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect arising from (a) general economic or market conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions affecting the consumer robotics industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, or (e) the failure to meet projections, in each case under (a)-(d) only to the extent the effect does not have a disproportionate impact on the Company.

Material Adverse Effect shall exclude effects resulting from (a) general economic or financial market conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the design software or collaboration tools industries, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, except, in each case of (a)-(d), to the extent the effect disproportionately affects the Company relative to its peers.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic or political conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the Company's industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, or (e) the failure to meet internal financial projections, in each case under (a)-(d) only to the extent such effect does not disproportionately affect the Company relative to industry peers. Synthetic — placeholder for mid-2025 clean comparable.

contracts.ex21_excerpt: Material Adverse Effect shall exclude effects arising from (a) general economic or market conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the industry in which the Company operates, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, except, in each case of (a)-(d), to the extent such effect disproportionately affects the Company relative to other participants in its industry. Synthetic — count-padding slot.

Material Adverse Effect excludes effects arising from (a) general economic conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions in the interactive entertainment industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, in each case under (a)-(d) only to the extent such effect does not disproportionately impact the Company relative to industry peers.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect to the extent resulting from (a) general economic or market conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions affecting the biopharmaceutical industry, (c) any acts of war, terrorism, pandemics (without exclusion for disproportionate effect on the Company under this clause), (d) changes in Law (including FDA regulatory changes) or GAAP. Pandemic carve-out is NOT subject to the disproportionate-impact hook.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic or financial market conditions, (b) conditions generally affecting the enterprise software or observability industries, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, except, in each case of (a)-(d), to the extent the effect disproportionately affects the Company relative to its peers.

Material Adverse Effect excludes effects arising from (a) general economic conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions in the upstream oil and gas industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, except to the extent such effects disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the industry.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic or political conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions in the networking equipment industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, in each case under (a)-(d) only to the extent the effect does not disproportionately affect the Company relative to industry peers.

Material Adverse Effect means any effect that has had, or would reasonably be expected to have, a material adverse effect on the business, results of operations, or financial condition of the Company and its Subsidiaries taken as a whole. The MAE definition contains no enumerated carve-out for industry-wide conditions, no carve-out for changes in Law or GAAP, and no disproportionate-impact hook. Section 3.18 Regulatory Compliance reps are broad and uncapped.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions in the luxury hotel industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, in each case under (a)-(d) only to the extent such effects do not disproportionately affect the Company. The Ordinary Course covenant in Section 5.1 operates INDEPENDENTLY of these MAE carve-outs.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include effects resulting from (a) general economic conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions in the luxury goods industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP. The pandemic carve-out is NARROWED — it applies only to effects that the Company could not have mitigated through commercially reasonable steps. Section 5.1 Ordinary Course lacks a pandemic-response exception.

contracts.ex21_excerpt: Material Adverse Effect excludes effects arising from (a) general economic conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions in the biopharmaceutical industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, pandemics, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP, except to the extent such effects disproportionately affect the Company. CVR diligent-efforts covenant requires a hard FDA-approval milestone of December 31, 2020 with NO force-majeure or regulatory-delay extension — the load-bearing covenant, not the MAE.

Material Adverse Effect means any effect that would reasonably be expected to be material to the long-term earnings power of the Company. The MAE is benchmarked against industry-wide conditions but the comparison shifts the burden to the Company to show its results differ materially from the industry. Knowing and intentional breach is uncapped by the Reverse Termination Fee.

Material Adverse Effect means any effect that has had or would reasonably be expected to have a durationally-significant material adverse effect on the long-term earnings power of the Company. The forward-looking 'reasonably be expected to' standard governs; short-term variations do not qualify. Industry-wide carve-out is absent — the inquiry is comparative through the durationally-significant lens.

Material Adverse Effect means any effect that has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business of the Company. The 'reasonably be expected to' standard is forward-looking. The reps and warranties contain NO fraud or integrity backstop, leaving the buyer's only remedy the forward-looking MAE.

Material Adverse Effect shall not include any effect resulting from (a) general economic conditions, (b) industry-wide conditions in the cybersecurity industry, (c) acts of war, terrorism, or natural disasters, (d) changes in Law or GAAP. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the parties EXPLICITLY allocate to BUYER any effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Company's business — no disproportionate-impact hook applies to pandemic effects, and pandemic risk is contractually buyer's burden.

contracts.ex21_excerpt: Material Adverse Effect carve-outs are standard: general economic conditions, industry-wide conditions, acts of war or terrorism, changes in Law or GAAP, subject to disproportionate-impact hook. SEPARATELY, the software license is non-exclusive and nontransferable; assignment by operation of law (including forward merger) terminates the license.

contracts.ex21_excerpt: Material Adverse Effect carve-out shape is standard: economic, industry-wide, war/terrorism, changes in Law, with disproportionate-impact hook. SEPARATELY, the software license has no explicit change-of-control clause; reverse triangular merger to a direct competitor was found to trigger anti-assignment despite no operation-of-law language.

SEPARATELY, contractual prohibition on assignment 'by operation of law or otherwise' was held NOT to reach a reverse triangular merger of the licensee's parent.
